title: Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance: adaptive scopes choose which users a policy covers (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, policy controls, role permissions and licensing statements are supported. The scope-creation route stops before the configuration choices, and the licence-check checklist item has no corresponding control row; these are minor findings.

claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": [ "General Availability" ]

claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2025.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2025"

claims.claim: The roadmap preview date is June CY2025.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "June CY2025"

claims.quote: "clouds": [ "GCC", "GCC High", "DoD" ]

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy; Scope
claims.claim: A Communication Compliance policy can use adaptive query scopes to choose the users or groups it covers.
claims.quote: Select adaptive scopes: An adaptive scope uses a query that you specify to define the membership of users or groups.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Adaptive scope queries run daily.
claims.quote: These dynamic queries run daily against the attributes or properties that you specify for the selected scope.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: User scopes can use Department, Country or region and Exchange CustomAttribute1-15 through attributes mapped to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Department ... Country or region ... Exchange custom attributes: CustomAttribute1 - CustomAttribute15 ... The attribute names for users and groups are based on filterable recipient properties that map to Microsoft Entra attributes.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Adaptive scoping is admin-opt-in: an administrator creates a scope and selects it for a policy rather than existing policies automatically changing selection.
claims.quote: To use an adaptive policy, create the adaptive scope before you create your policy, then select the scope when you choose this option.

claims.claim: Choose users and reviewers offers All users, Select users and Select adaptive scopes under Choose users and groups.
claims.quote: On the Choose users and reviewers page: ... In the Choose users and groups section, select one of the following options: ... All users ... Select users ... Select adaptive scopes

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to create the adaptive scopes before creating the adaptive policy.
claims.quote: If you decide to create an adaptive policy, you must create one or more adaptive scopes before you create your policy, and then select them when you choose this option.

claims.claim: Adaptive scopes have a simple query builder for supported attributes.
claims.quote: You can easily specify the attributes and properties listed in the table when you configure an adaptive scope by using the simple query builder.

claims.claim: The advanced query builder uses OPATH filters for User and Microsoft 365 Group scopes.
claims.quote: For User and Microsoft 365 Group scopes: Use OPATH filtering syntax.

claims.claim: Site scopes do not apply to Communication Compliance.
claims.quote: Site scopes aren't applicable to Communication Compliance so you won't see them when you add a scope.

claims.claim: Communication Compliance adaptive policies support excluded users and Microsoft 365 groups.
claims.quote: For communication compliance policies: ... Excluded users and Microsoft 365 groups are supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: An adaptive scope is reusable across Communication Compliance, retention and auto-labeling policies, making its query shared configuration.
claims.quote: When you create a communication compliance policy, a policy for retention, or an auto-labeling policy, you can add an adaptive scope for your policy. ... As a reusable configuration element, the same adaptive scope can be used for other compliance policies.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Changing queried directory attributes changes whether a user matches the adaptive scope.
claims.quote: Once daily, this query runs against Entra ID and identifies all users who have the value Europe specified for in their account for the Country or region attribute.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Queries can take up to five days to populate fully, so Microsoft advises waiting a few days before attaching a new scope to a policy.
claims.quote: It can take up to five days for the queries to fully populate and changes aren't immediate. Factor in this delay by waiting a few days before you add a newly created scope to a policy.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Purview does not immediately validate whether the typed query value is correct.
claims.quote: Because the query doesn't run immediately, there's no validation that you typed in the value correctly.

claims.claim: Policy user scope determines whose communications are identified for reviewers, subject to the policy's locations and conditions.
claims.quote: Use Communication Compliance policies to identify user communications for analysis by internal or external reviewers.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Any role group with Scope Manager can create scopes, including Compliance Administrator, Compliance Data Administrator, Organization Management, Records Management, Communication Compliance and Communication Compliance Admins.
claims.quote: Any role group with the Scope Manager role can create an adaptive scope. ... Compliance Administrator ... Compliance Data Administrator ... Organization Management ... Records Management ... Communication Compliance ... Communication Compliance Admins

claims.claim: Select adaptive scopes is hidden if the policy is scoped by administrative units.

claims.claim: Users without a valid adaptive-scope licence do not have policy settings applied to them.

claims.claim: The Show insights and recommendations blind-spot checkbox is unavailable with adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: This setting isn't available if you choose the All users option or the Select adaptive scopes option.

claims.claim: Adaptive scoping is an included option within the licensed Communication Compliance product.

claims.claim: The Get started page requires a supported organizational subscription and appropriate licences assigned to users.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate adaptive-scoping licence line or charge is published for Communication Compliance.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview adaptive scopes separate pricing meter charge' and 'Communication Compliance adaptive scopes license licensing valid license adaptive scopes'; read Adaptive scopes, Get started, and the service description's Communication Compliance table; no separate scope charge or licence.

claims.claim: Detecting inappropriate or risky interactions in non-Microsoft 365 AI data requires enabling pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: To detect inappropriate or risky interactions for non-Microsoft 365 AI data, you need to enable pay-as-you-go billing in your organization.

claims.claim: The Get started page states there are no pay-as-you-go requirements or charges for detecting risky interactions in Microsoft 365 Copilot data.
claims.quote: There aren't any pay-as-you-go billing requirements or charges for Microsoft 365 detecting inappropriate or risky interaction for Microsoft 365 Copilot data.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Not yet published; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft does not separately identify which licence its phrase 'a valid license for adaptive scopes' means for Communication Compliance.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Communication Compliance adaptive scopes license licensing valid license adaptive scopes'; read Adaptive scopes and the service description. The former uses the phrase without naming a SKU; the latter names Communication Compliance plans, not a distinct adaptive-scope entitlement for it.

claims.quote: Number of groups: 10

claims.claim: Get-Recipient with -Filter in Exchange Online PowerShell can validate an adaptive query.
claims.quote: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell ... Use either Get-Recipient, Get-Mailbox, or Get-User with the -Filter parameter and your OPATH query for the adaptive scope enclosed in curly brackets

claims.claim: Get-Mailbox with -Filter in Exchange Online PowerShell can validate an adaptive query.
claims.quote: Use either Get-Recipient, Get-Mailbox, or Get-User with the -Filter parameter and your OPATH query ... You can determine whether to use Get-Mailbox, Get-Recipient, or Get-User for validation by identifying which cmdlet is supported by the OPATH property

claims.claim: Scope details shows Removed in the State column for former members that no longer match the query.
claims.quote: Review the State column in the list that shows Added for members within the adaptive scope or Removed if the member was previously in the adaptive scope but removed now they no longer match the scope query.

claims.claim: The Purview route to selecting adaptive scopes is Communication Compliance > Policies > Create policy > Custom policy > Choose users and reviewers > Choose users and groups > Select adaptive scopes.
claims.quote: Go to the Communication Compliance solution. ... Select Policies ... Select Create policy, then select Custom policy. ... On the Choose users and reviewers page: ... In the Choose users and groups section ... Select adaptive scopes

claims.claim: No sufficiently documented automation operation selects adaptive scopes for a Communication Compliance policy.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Communication Compliance assign adaptive scope PowerShell IncludeAdaptiveScopes Set-SupervisoryReviewRule'; opened New- and Set-SupervisoryReviewRule: both leave the parameter description unfilled. Get started says policies must be managed through the solution, not PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; rendered table
claims.claim: Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope is the Purview route to creating a scope.
claims.quote: Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes. ... select + Create scope. ... first asked to assign an administrative unit. ... keep the default of Full directory. ... Select the type of scope, and then select the attributes or properties
claims.fix: The route correctly opens creation but stops before its configuration choices. Keep 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes > + Create scope' and append to the row note: 'In the wizard, choose Full directory or an assigned administrative unit, select Users or Microsoft 365 Groups, then select the attributes and enter their values.' Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-adaptive-scopes.

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <String> -LocationType User -FilterConditions <PswsHashtable> creates a user adaptive scope with query conditions.
claims.quote: New-AdaptiveScope -Name <String> -FilterConditions <PswsHashtable> -LocationType <DynamicBoundaryLocationType> ... The FilterConditions parameter specifies the conditions that are included in the dynamic boundary.

claims.claim: Purview Settings > Roles and groups > Role groups > role group > Edit > Choose users assigns role-group members.
claims.quote: Select Settings ... select Roles and groups, then select Role groups ... Select the Communication Compliance role group, then select Edit. ... Select Choose users

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to a role group.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.quote: Use the Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers cmdlet to retrieve current and past members of adaptive scopes in your organization. ... Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers [-Identity] <ComplianceRuleIdParameter>

claims.claim: The portal membership details list shows at most 1 million members.
claims.quote: The adaptive scope can apply to more than 1 million members. However, the member details can only show up to 1 million members across both added and removed members.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs administrators to Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers for scope membership of 1,000 or more.
claims.quote: If the scope membership is large (1,000 or more), or you want to customize the export, use the PowerShell cmdlet Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers.

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope also accepts Group for LocationType.
claims.quote: The LocationType parameter specifies the location where the adaptive scope filter is defined. Valid values are: ... User ... Group (Microsoft 365 group) ... Site

claims.claim: The New-SupervisoryReviewRule reference lists IncludeAdaptiveScopes as String[] but does not explain its effect or accepted scope identifiers.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Communication Compliance assign adaptive scope PowerShell IncludeAdaptiveScopes Set-SupervisoryReviewRule'; opened the New-SupervisoryReviewRule reference: syntax includes [-IncludeAdaptiveScopes <String[]>], but its description is '{{ Fill IncludeAdaptiveScopes Description }}'.

claims.claim: The Get-AdaptiveScopeMembers reference describes retention and Insider Risk Management uses rather than explicitly naming Communication Compliance.
claims.quote: Adaptive scopes are used in retention policies, Insider Risk Management policies and retention label policies.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The governance checklist's instruction to check assigned user licences has a corresponding control in the controls table.
claims.quote: 'Confirm that matched users hold a licence that includes Communication Compliance'; the table covers policy scope selection, scope creation, role-group membership and scope-member reporting, not licence assignment.
claims.fix: The After rollout instruction to check assigned licences has no corresponding control row. Remove that checklist bullet; retain the verified user-licensing requirement in Cost and licensing and the unlicensed-user limitation in Risk assessment.

claims.claim: The sources do not specify whether a newly matched user's earlier messages are evaluated retrospectively.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Communication Compliance adaptive scope new member messages evaluated prior added scope'; searched the policies article for adaptive scoping and read its user-selection section, the Get started steps and Adaptive scopes. No passage specifies retrospective evaluation for new scope members.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Adaptive scope query changes can take up to five days to become effective and appear in Scope details.
claims.quote: Adaptive scope query changes can take up to five days to become effective and reflected in the scope details view of the Adaptive Scopes page.

claims.claim: New-AdaptiveScope is available in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: The New-AdaptiveScope reference describes retention uses rather than explicitly naming Communication Compliance.
claims.quote: Use the New-AdaptiveScope cmdlet to create adaptive scopes in your organization. Adaptive scopes (or static scopes) are used in retention policies and retention label policies.
